findings.note: Named as one of three primary sponsors (Hise, Daniel, P. Newton) of SB 921, Const. Am./Require Photo ID For All Voters. The bill text says it amends Article VI of the state constitution so that all voters, not just those voting in person, must present photographic identification before voting, and puts the question to voters on November 3, 2026. The bill was ratified 12/13/2024 (S.L. 2024-58).

findings.note: Named as one of three primary sponsors (Hise, P. Newton, Daniel) of SB 747, Elections Law Changes. The bill text includes ID provisions: photo identification for same-day registration, a list of documents accepted as proof for mail registrants, a photocopy of ID or a sworn affidavit with absentee ballots, and a rule that a voter who does not present photo ID may be challenged. It also has provisions on jury-duty excusals of non-citizens being passed to the State Board of Elections. It became law over a veto as S.L. 2023-140.

findings.note: Named as the first of three primary sponsors (Daniel, McKissick, Hise) of SB 683, Combat Absentee Ballot Fraud. The bill text has the State Board set the forms of identification sent with a written request for an absentee ballot, and a reasonable-impediment process (such as a license number, special ID card number or last four digits of the Social Security number) for a voter who cannot attach a copy. It became law as S.L. 2019-239 on 11/6/2019.

findings.note: Named as the first of three primary sponsors (Daniel, Newton, Hise) of SB 326, Election Integrity Act. The bill text includes an appropriation of five million dollars to set up a program to identify people who need photo ID to vote in person, with a mobile component to visit them. It also moves absentee-ballot request and receipt dates and bars private money for election offices. The bill page shows it vetoed.
